attrs.evidence: GPT-5.6’s INV-R9.2 audit §7, measured against the implementation. scripts/integration-delta.mjs already computes dropped_ids and removed_files; nothing consumes them. candidatePopulation disposes candidate_ids only and filePopulation changed_files only, so a source deletion is not a candidate and not a file disposition. The collision test reads pL.has(k) && pL.get(k) !== baseline, so a canonical DELETION of a shared record is not a dual-lane change. For the INV-R7.5 instance every one of these is zero, which is why the instance stands — and zero is exactly why nobody noticed.
attrs.gap: NOT IMPLEMENTED, and deliberately not implemented here. The full deletion algebra needs a disposition vocabulary of its own (a deletion may be adopted, refused, or collide with a target modification) and INV-R9.3 was scoped to close the two blockers before Phase D. This must close before the NEXT cross-lane integration, which is Δ(next frozen R7.x − INV-R7.5), and that delta will not be all-additions.
attrs.review_focus: Is a deletion a disposition of the SOURCE’s act, or of the TARGET’s decision not to keep something? The two give different vocabularies.
attrs.statement: An integration disposition domain must cover source-lane and canonical-lane DELETIONS — dropped claim records, removed paths, and delete-versus-modify collisions — not only additions and modifications.
